document.title: Focus ranges and lettered line notes inside hunks
document.summary: Groups gain `focus` ranges and up to three line `notes`. `validate` checks them against live hunks, `refresh` carries them, `show` prints line numbers to copy, and the group view opens a focused hunk on its range with lettered note pins.
document.why: [PR #170](source:s2) says reviewers read long hunks top to bottom and lose the few lines that matter, and that context about a line has nowhere to live except group prose.

sources.title: Focus ranges and line notes inside hunks
sources.gist: Asks for per-group focus ranges and notes, loud validate checks, a collapsed hunk view, refresh rules per hunk status, and numbered show output.

sources.label: PR #170
sources.gist: Implements #163 on main beside group attention and questions, and lists its decisions for review.

lookFor: [#163](source:s1) gives refresh rules for `same`, `changed`, and `gone` hunks. At head, `carryAnchors` also drops a range or note on a `reformat` hunk and counts it with the `changed` ones in the report. [PR #170](source:s2) gives the reason: whitespace edits can move lines inside the hunk.

[#163](source:s1) puts the caption and `Showing 12 of 48 lines · Show whole hunk` above a focused hunk. At head, the bar above the hunk holds the caption and the toggle, and the line counts move into rows at each cut edge inside the diff (`⋯ N lines above not shown`). No source gives the reason for the move.

groups.title: Focus and note fields
groups.why: [#163](source:s1) asks for `focus` ranges and `notes` on each group. The later groups read these fields.
groups.summary: `review.ts` adds `focus` and `notes` to the group schema, and `anchor.ts` finds the live hunk that holds a range or a note.

attention.note: The 25-line cap, `end >= start`, and the three-note cap are zod checks in `review.ts`. So `serve` and `export` also refuse a document that breaks them, not only `validate`. Decide whether a bad range should block `serve`.

groups.title: validate and refresh
groups.why: [#163](source:s1) asks `validate` to fail loudly on a range or note outside its hunk, and `refresh` to carry each one by hunk status.
groups.summary: `cmdValidate` adds `anchorErrors` from `anchors.ts`, and `refreshDocument` calls `carryAnchors` to shift or drop each anchor.

attention.note: `carryAnchors` keeps an anchor only on a `same` hunk. A whitespace-only push makes the hunk `reformat`, so its ranges and notes drop, and the agent writes them again. Decide whether that loss is worth the safety.

notes.body: Each drop here adds to `changed`, which `formatRefresh` in `refresh.ts` prints as `1 focus range dropped` on the group's report line.

groups.title: Numbered show
groups.why: [#163](source:s1) asks `show` to print old and new line numbers, so the agent copies numbers instead of counting from the `@@` header.
groups.summary: `cmdShow` prints `numberedPatch` from `show.ts`, which numbers the raw hunk text and keeps git's no-newline marker.

groups.title: Collapsed hunk and note pins
groups.why: [#163](source:s1) asks a focused hunk to open on its range with one click to the whole hunk, and notes to show as lettered agent notes.
groups.summary: `focusBlocks` in `focus.ts` turns a focused file into bars, diffs, and hidden-lines rows, which `HunkView` renders with `FocusBar`, `HiddenLines`, and one `PierreFileDiff` per diff; `NotePin` adds the lettered note rows.

attention.note: A file with a focus range renders one diff per block, with `hydrate` off and plain separator bars. Its gaps between hunks no longer expand, even after "Show whole hunk". Decide whether that cost is right for focused files.

questions: Why does `focusBlocks` render the file whole, with no mark, when the patch's `@@` lines do not line up with its hunks?

groups.title: Eval grading
groups.why: [#163](source:s1) asks for rubric lines for focus ranges and notes.
groups.summary: `packet.ts` lists each group's ranges and notes for the grader, `graders.ts` checks each caption and note at head, and three `expected.md` files gain rubric lines.

groups.title: Skill and glossary
groups.why: [#163](source:s1) asks the skill to say when to write a focus range or a note, and the glossary to define both.
groups.summary: A Focus and notes section in `SKILL.md` names when to write each one, and `example.md` and the glossary show both beside attention and questions.

groups.title: Synced copies and generated schema
groups.why: `pnpm sync:skill` and `pnpm generate:schema` write these files from the skill source and `review.ts`.
groups.summary: The `.agents` skill files copy `skills-next`, and the three `review.schema.json` files come from `review.ts`, so the reader can skip them.

commits.subject: Show the cut in the diff and the focus reason as a reason
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
A focused file renders hunk by hunk: each Agent focus bar sits on its
hunk, and a hidden-lines row at each cut edge counts the lines not shown,
names the notes it hides, and opens the whole hunk. The skill asks the
caption to say why to read the lines, gives an added file no range, and
asks captions and notes to add a fact the summary and attention lack.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Review round 1: an all-insertion excerpt of a new file wrote a -1 start; a
range starting mid-block missed the deletions it replaces; an anchor on
context a same hunk shed survived refresh and failed validate; show lost
git's no-newline marker.

commits.subject: Focus ranges and line notes inside hunks
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Groups gain focus (a range inside one live hunk, at most 25 lines, with a
caption) and notes (line-anchored, at most 3). validate fails a range or
note outside its group's live hunks. refresh shifts them with a same hunk
and drops them with a changed or gone one. show prints old and new line
numbers. The UI opens a focused hunk on its range with a Show whole hunk
toggle and letters notes A, B, C as Pierre line annotations.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>
